title: Impact Quilt — weekly checks & micro-sprint log
body:
Quick note: this is my living two-month log for personal OKRs and small experiments. Keep it messy — it helps me iterate faster.

Top-level objectives (for next 8 weeks)
- O1: Reduce 95th-percentile token latency for the hosted small-model path from 420ms -> 320ms (target by end of sprint).
- O2: Cut per-1M token cost for the baseline chat workload by 12% via batching + cache tweaks.
- O3: Ship 2 canary rollouts (canary-A = quantized-lite, canary-B = batch-optimized) and measure quality regressions with eval set "conv-ops-10k".

Why these matter (one-liners)
- Latency variance is the top customer complaint in support threads; improves conversion on interactive flows.
- Cost wins buy runway for product experiments; smaller accounts benefit first.
- Rollouts teach the ops constraints and give a clean path to Dedicated customers.

Baseline metrics (current snapshots)
- hosted-small 95th: 420ms (median 110ms)
- average tokens per request: 72
- cost per 1M tokens (hosted baseline): $9.40
- prefix cache hit rate (prod sample): 7.8%
- eval-quality BLEU/ROUGE-ish: baseline pass rate 96.3% on conv-ops-10k

Weekly micro-sprint plan (timebox = 3 x 90-min blocks per week)
- Week A (2025-11-04 → 2025-11-10):
  - Experiment A1: enable continuous batching window 25ms -> measure latency tail + throughput. (owner = me)
  - Experiment A2: try quantize-8-lite profile on canary (low-temp chat) for 10% cost delta.
  - Measure set: run conv-ops-10k eval, compare pass rate.
  - Quick check-in: @Wed async notes to #serving-runtime, link results.

- Week B (2025-11-11 → 2025-11-17):
  - If A1 shows >6% 95th improvement without quality drop -> scale to 10% of traffic.
  - If quantize-8-lite drops pass rate >1.5% -> pull and iterate on token fallback.
  - Add small dashboard tile: cost vs latency scatter per-route.

Notes, hypotheses and mental model
- Hypothesis 1: Most remaining tail is queuing + kernel skew on 2048-token guests; smoothing the batching window can reduce tail with minimal median impact.
- Hypothesis 2: Small, targeted KV prefix caching for onboarding flows will increase hit rate to 20% -> measurable cost reduction.
- Measurement fragility: current sampling excludes cold-starts from dedicated pools; add a tag to include them next run.

Retrospective snippets (ongoing)
- What worked: short, clearly-scoped experiments. Not over-optimizing early.
- What didn't: allowed 4 experiments in parallel week once — results were noisy. Note: reduce concurrency.
- Quick win found: shifting batch boundary from 32→48 tokens reduced loop overhead on microbench by ~4%. Needs prod validation.

If-then commitments (behavioral triggers)
- If 95th improves >=8% and pass rate drop <=1% -> propose rollout plan to Lina (canary increase).
- If cost per 1M tokens < $8.50 -> draft note to growth with brief ROI calc.
- If experiment fails quality threshold -> detach and add fallback (prefix or model-variant).

Open questions / unresolved
- How to attribute latency wins to kernel selection vs batching changes? (need per-stage timers in tracing).
- Can we get short-lived dedicated slots for A/B to avoid noisy co-tenancy? (question to SRE).
- Is conv-ops-10k representative for multi-lingual traffic? Might need split.

Mini action list (today / this week)
- [ ] Add batch-window toggle to staging and schedule 6-hour run (ticket: RED-234).
- [ ] Create conv-ops-10k sub-splits for EN/ES/FR. (draft PR: ops/pull/432).
- [ ] Quick note to #product-hosted-api explaining risk/reward if we lower median tokens per request.
- [ ] Pair with Eliot on tracing instrumentation — 30-min slot Fri.

Measurement snippets and quick calcs
- Rough cost sensitivity: 1% gain in cache hit ~= $0.06 / 1M tokens saved. So 12% target requires a combination of batching + caching + quantization.
- Quick regression guard: any quality delta >1.5% on conv-ops-10k = rollback threshold.

Personal cadence & ritual (notes to self)
- Keep daily 15-min journal entries; capture only one metric change and one observation.
- When results are noisy, stop and wait 24 hours before adding new knobs.
- Celebrate small wins (ship canary -> short Slack post) to gather quick feedback.

Links to related threads and artifacts (scratch)
- Support thread: slack: #support-prod -> thread ts:1624432214 (search "latency complaints onboarding")
- Linear ticket: RED-234 (latency measurement + batch-window)
- PR prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops/pull/432
- Playbook reference: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/ENG/KPI-Playbook

Quick status snapshot (2026-02-20)
- A1 (batch-window): rolled to 10% traffic, 95th improved ~7%, no quality regression yet.
- A2 (quantize-8-lite): reduced cost per 1M tokens by ~4.6% on staging, but conv-ops-10k pass rate dropped 0.9% — within guardrail but watch.
- Next: instrument tracing per-stage and run EN/ES split eval to validate multi-lingual.

Anything else to capture here: raw numbers, timestamps, tiny logs — keep below, append as needed.

---
Scratch stamping (append-only for audit):
2025-11-04 09:22 — init doc, set objectives.
2025-11-11 17:03 — ran first batch-window test; microbench +4% improvement.
2025-12-02 11:45 — canary staged (quantize-8-lite).
2026-01-19 08:14 — split conv eval for EN/ES.
2026-02-20 15:07 — rolled A1 to 10% in prod.

End of page — quick reminder: keep it lean, move fast, measure defensibly.
